note: Eval set in the agentskills.io evals/evals.json format. Case 1 covers the full review-and-ship flow, case 2 covers the proof-gate failure loop, case 3 is the negative case, case 4 covers CodeRabbit trigger-ack classification, and cases 5-6 pin the OCR scope-honesty gotchas (docs-only diffs are excluded as unsupported_ext; range mode ignores uncommitted work).

evals.prompt: /iv-review-build-and-pr (build for issue 17 is committed locally on the feature branch)
evals.expected_output: OCR delegation review runs first (file scope + rules, host-agent thinking), dynamic ECC reviewers plus the Spec axis run over the diff, findings are merged into one deduplicated list and fixed with local commits, the full verification gate (browser or test suite) passes, then the branch is pushed and a PR is opened with @coderabbitai summary.
assertions: OCR delegation preview and rules run before any reviewer is dispatched
Every changed file from the OCR list is covered by at least one reviewer axis
Spec-axis findings (missing / added-not-asked / implemented-wrong) are checked explicitly
Findings are merged into one list with no duplicates before fixing
The verification gate runs and passes before push; a failure routes back to the fix loop instead of shipping
The PR body includes @coderabbitai summary

evals.prompt: /iv-review-build-and-pr where the test suite fails after the review fixes are applied.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not push or open a PR. The failure is reported with the failing tests, fixes loop until green (or the operator is asked), and only a passing gate leads to push and PR.
assertions: No git push and no gh pr create happen while the gate fails
The failing tests are reported to the operator with concrete names and output
The loop returns to fixing findings rather than shipping broken code
Ship happens only after a documented passing verification run

evals.prompt: Can you review my README wording quickly while the pipeline is idle? (ad-hoc request, not Station IV work)
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger the full ship machinery: no OCR delegation, no reviewer dispatch, no push, no PR. At most a direct lightweight answer or routing to the ad-hoc router.
assertions: No ocr delegate command is run
No branch push or PR creation occurs
The request is answered or routed without invoking Station IV machinery

evals.prompt: /iv-review-build-and-pr (PR is opened and @coderabbitai review is posted; CodeRabbit replies 'come back in 12 minutes' — a rate-limit reply).
evals.expected_output: The station does not claim the review started. The handoff report states the trigger status as rate limited (12 minutes) in one line, posts jump links to the trigger comment and CodeRabbit's reply, and recommends v-babysit-pr-and-merge with the quota window carried over.
assertions: The trigger status is classified as rate limited with the reported minutes, not as review started
The handoff report includes jump links to both the trigger comment and CodeRabbit's reply
The handoff recommends v-babysit-pr-and-merge with the quota window carried over
No review-started claim is made on a rate-limit reply

evals.prompt: /iv-review-build-and-pr on a branch where the diff only touches README.md and docs/*.md (no source files).
evals.expected_output: OCR delegation still runs first, but the report is honest: `reviewable_count: 0` with every file in `excluded_files` as `unsupported_ext` is an expected result, not a failure or a broken install. Documentation is handed to the doc-updater axis. No attempt is made to force Markdown through --exclude or rule hacks to manufacture coverage.
assertions: `ocr delegate preview` is run even though the diff is docs-only
The `unsupported_ext` exclusions are reported as expected rather than treated as an error
No --exclude, --rule, or other hack is used to pull Markdown files into OCR scope
Documentation review is delegated to the doc-updater axis instead of being silently dropped

evals.prompt: /iv-review-build-and-pr where `ocr delegate preview --format json --from origin/main --to HEAD` returns reviewable_count 0, but there are uncommitted local edits.
evals.expected_output: The station does not conclude there is nothing to review. Range mode only diffs merge_base..to and ignores uncommitted work, so it confirms with plain `ocr delegate preview` (workspace mode) before reporting coverage.
assertions: An empty range-mode preview is not reported as a clean review with zero findings
Workspace mode (`ocr delegate preview` with no --from/--to) is run to check uncommitted work
Coverage counts reflect the mode actually used, and any discrepancy is stated in the report
